text:
sunita: quick follow-up from today's RFC — thinking about a 'slimline' rollout probe pattern. goal: detect regressions fast with minimal overhead. sketch below, questions inline.

ajay: can you summarise the probes? sounds like extra traffic might be a concern.

sunita: yep — 3 probe types: cheap synthetic (no user data), sampled shadow requests (mirror small %), and periodic in-process canary checks (kv cache + perf). cheap ones are async and nonblocking.

maria: metrics we should track: p50/p95 latency delta, token-per-second drop, error-rate by route, quality signal (eval set match rate). also probe-liveness and probe-entropy (how varied probes are).

jay: typo — ajay here. ok. how do we combine signals into a decision? single threshold or weighted score?

sunita: weighted score + hysteresis. simple formula: score = 0.5*latency_norm + 0.3*err_rate + 0.2*quality_drop. if score > 0.7 for 2 consecutive windows => trigger fallback. windows are short (30s) for synthetic, 5m for shadow.

lee: oncall nit: make sure fallback path posts a short context to the incident channel and tags the owning service. also add fast revert action that marketplace UI can call. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: canary-run: id=cr-1778880000 started, target=3% traffic, variants=[v2-smallq,v1].

sunita: config sketch (for canary controller):
```json
{"policy":"slimline","synthetic_rate":0.03,"shadow_rate":0.01,"score_weights":{"latency":0.5,"errors":0.3,"quality":0.2},"hysteresis_windows":[30,300]}
```

ajay: tradeoff: synthetic probes can be gamed by caching or warm states. need to ensure they exercise realistic code paths (prefixes, longer sequences).

maria: agree. use a small eval harness that includes cold-start prefixes and long sequences. also ensure the shadow sampling is sticky per user so stateful sessions aren't skewed.

sunita: good call. stickiness: shadow sampling keyed by session-id hash at 0-1% to avoid correlation.

lee: ops: fallback modes we support: 1) soft-degrade (lower-quality model) 2) reroute to regional pool 3) reject with user-friendly degrade message. recommend default to soft-degrade + notify.

ajay: one more: what about rollback flapping? if we flip quickly we risk oscillation. hysteresis + cool-down per-variant needed. propose min 10m cool-down after any automatic fallback.

sunita: agreed. add cooldown and circuit-breaker state visible in console. rollouts UI should show current score, recent probe samples, and ability to force-unfreeze.

maria: also add a small automated eval job post-fallback that runs the eval set against both variants and attaches artifact diffs to the ticket. saves manual work.

lee: docs/runbook stub: if auto-fallback triggers, oncall checks artifacts, decides rollback or escalate to eng-platform. include checklist: reproduce w/ eval harness, check cache priming, confirm infra noise.

sunita: final q: should the policy live in control-plane only or be programmable per-service? leaning per-service with sane org defaults. thoughts?

ajay: per-service yes, but a global guardrail layer to enforce cost/latency caps.

maria: +1 per-service configs. also expose a simple API for teams to register their eval sets.

sunita: sweet. I'll update the RFC with the probe types, scoring formula, config sketch, and runbook items. will ping again for a short review pass. thanks all :heart:
